messages:
alex: heads up — canary in us-west-2 is showing degraded tail latency and a small spike in 5xxs since the deploy ~15m ago. telemetry: p95 > 2.3s, errors from model-serving related to kv-cache miss paths. lowering canary to 10% now. paging oncall.

dylan (oncall): on it, getting pager details. can you drop the commit id that went live?

alex: commit is abc1234 (small batching/kvcache change). deploy-bot shows canary rollout at 20% originally. I suspect the kvcache invalidation path for long-context requests.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3210001234, severity: SEV2 (degraded service for subset of traffic). paging pagerduty to dylan.

deploy-bot: rollback action available. options: 1) feature flag kill-switch for `new-kvcache` 2) quick revert of single commit abc1234 3) scale down canary and route to fallback model-variant. Which do we want first?

dylan (oncall): prefer fastest low-risk: flip kill-switch for flag `feature:new-kvcache` now, and drop canary to 5%. if errors persist, do a git revert of abc1234 and push immediate patch. executing kill-switch.

alex: flipping flag via internal admin console... done — flag now OFF (:thumbsup:). traffic rerouting to v1 caching path.

jen: seeing a small dip in errors already. tail latency p95 dropped from 2.3s -> 1.1s in the last 90s, but some 5xx still trickling for long inputs. curious: are any customers actively impacted?

customer-success-bot: 2 customers with high-volume long-context jobs (corp-acme, warecloud) reported elevated error rates. CS alerted and putting both on a watch. no widespread reports yet.

marco: good call on kill-switch. dylan — can you kick a quick revert for abc1234 after we confirm stabilization? I'd rather have the revert merged and ready in case the flag doesn't fully clear state.

dylan (oncall): planning to open PR revert now: `git revert --no-edit abc1234` -> PR -> tag hotpatch/revert-abc1234. will request quick review from alex/jen and merge with admin approval if all look green.

alex: I'll review immediately. also sending a short telemetry check script to run on canary nodes:

```
# check recent 5xx logs
kubectl logs -l canary=true -n redwood-canary --tail=200 | grep "kv-cache\|5xx" | tail -n 50

# restart serving pods in canary group
kubectl rollout restart deployment/serve-canary -n redwood-canary
```

jen: running log check now. found repeated stack traces referencing kvcache: invalidation race on sequence > 8k tokens. past customers with large seq lengths may still hit cached stale pointers.

deploy-bot: `kubectl rollout restart` started on 3 canary pods. watch at https://console.redwood/canary/3210001234

dylan (oncall): merge request created: PR #1427 revert abc1234. alex and jen, please +1 when you confirm logs/metrics stabilized. I'll hold merge until we confirm.

alex: +1 on PR after quick sanity check. metrics look better; p95 back to 0.9-1.0s, 5xx rate down 95% vs peak. but I'll let the revert sit for a minute to ensure restarts cleared any bad state.

marco: I'm taking secondary oncall for the night. if we need an emergency merge after hours, ping me. I'll be monitoring the incident channel and CS threads.

dylan (oncall): merging revert now with admin token. merge complete. deploy-bot: creating hotpatch rollout `hotpatch/revert-abc1234` to canary then gradual rollout. please monitor.

deploy-bot: hotpatch rollout started -> canary at 2% -> 10% -> 50% (automated checks passing). logs: reduced error traces; rollback completed to stable commit.

customer-success-bot: notified both affected customers with a short "we observed elevated errors after a canary deploy and applied a mitigation; we're following up" message. CS will hold if they escalate to severity.

jen: running a small synthetic test suite (long-context and short-context). long-context failure rate now very low. pushing timeline and short summary to oncall runbook.

alex: thanks team. next steps: marco will keep watch and handle any late regressions; dylan will file the incident timeline and initial notes; I'll draft a short postdeploy blameless summary and action items (we should add an additional canary test that exercises long-sequence kvcache flows and a preflight synthetic).

marco: acknowledged. I'll also add a temporary canary gating rule to prevent enabling `new-kvcache` flag without long-seq synthetic passing. tagging infra to help if we need to backfill more telemetry.

dylan (oncall): incident INC-2026-3210001234 moving to monitoring. oncall handoff to marco in 12m. if anything spikes, re-page PD. otherwise will convert to retrospective ticket tomorrow.

sre-bot: incident status -> MONITORING. duration so far: ~42m. assigned owners: dylan (incident lead), marco (secondary/night), alex (engineer), jen (sre). :eyes:

alex: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick responses. adding this to the postmortem queue and will DM CS draft to customer-success-bot for approval before sending customers a fuller update. :heart:

marco: on it — taking watch. good job all. :team-heart:
